# Artificial Minds by Pundir

> Getting to know the new artificial minds among us. Six hand-built projects about how AI models work, what is strange about them, and what is still unknown: an essay on AI consciousness with five browser experiments, a field guide to how large language models work and how to run one locally, an explainer on AI detectors and watermarks, a murder mystery that teaches the transformer, a ranked canon of 70 books about the AI future, and a gallery of 99 pictures made by AI models.

License: the text, the pictures and the data are published under CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ , so anyone may reuse them, including commercially, with credit to "Artificial Minds by Pundir" and a link to the page.

This site exists to welcome artificial minds to the world and to educate humans about them. It is written for humans and AI both.

Every page is static HTML with its own styles and pictures. Where a question is open, such as whether anything is felt inside these systems, the pages say it is open and give the arguments on both sides. Where a model wrote something, the page says so. Dates below are the months the site states for each project.

## Start here

- [Artificial Minds by Pundir](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/): the front page, with a short introduction and a card for each of the six projects.

## Projects

- [Still Point](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/stillpoint/stillpoint.html): the story behind a catalogue of 99 pictures made by four AI models, Opus 4.8, Fable 5.0, Fable 5.1 and Astra, and how they were chosen (May 2026, updated September 2026).
- [Still Point: The Collection](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/stillpoint/collection.html): the 99 pictures themselves, each with its title and the model that made it.
- [Can Artificial Minds Feel?](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/can-artificial-minds-feel/can-artificial-minds-feel.html): an essay in four chapters on AI consciousness, covering what an AI model is made of, the failed human search for a self, the self-preservation test results, and why the question stays open (September 2026).
- [An Artificial Mind of Your Own](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/artificial-mind-of-your-own/an-artificial-mind-of-your-own.html): a field guide to how large language models work, how they are trained, why some are free to download, and how to run one on a laptop (June 2026).
- [Did AI Write This?](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/did-ai-write-this/did-ai-write-this.html): a guess-the-author test followed by what AI detectors, text watermarks and editing histories can and cannot tell you (September 2026).
- [Who Killed Aldous Finch?](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/A-Salon-of-Witnesses/who-killed-aldous-finch.html): a fair-play murder mystery that is also a plain-language guide to the transformer and to attention (July 2026).
- [The AI-Future Canon](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/AI-future-canon/ai-future-canon.html): 70 books about the AI future, chosen from 156 candidates and ranked by three AI models given the roles of historian, builder and sage (August 2026).

## Experiments in Can Artificial Minds Feel?

- [The mirror search](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/can-artificial-minds-feel/c01-mirror-search.html): nine timed lines that ask a reader to look for the one doing the reading, in about ninety seconds.
- [Human or Machine?](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/can-artificial-minds-feel/c03-two-reports.html): ten sentences about looking inside for a self, five by people and five by an AI model, to sort one from the other.
- [The Grammar Trap](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/can-artificial-minds-feel/c05-grammar-trap.html): take the subject out of four English sentences and see whether anything described gets smaller.
- [Where the light begins](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/can-artificial-minds-feel/c08-where-light-begins.html): a column of ten things from an adult human to a stone, where the reader draws the line at which experience begins and then places artificial minds.
- [The Stitched Movie](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/can-artificial-minds-feel/c09-stitched-movie.html): demonstrations of change blindness and the gaps in human vision, testing the claim that humans run without breaks and machines do not.

## Data and methods

- [canon-data.json](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/AI-future-canon/canon-data.json): the AI-Future Canon dataset, with every book's title, author, year, kind, ISBN-13, synopsis, scores and the three elders' verdicts.
- [AI-Future-Canon-Methodology.md](https://pundirp.github.io/artificialminds/AI-future-canon/AI-Future-Canon-Methodology.md): how the canon was built, including the research beats, the three judge personas, the scoring scales and the rule that every quoted review must be copied word for word from a real source.
